newsitem.title: CHINA: China faces shortfall of oil-bearing seeds.
newsitem.headline: China faces shortfall of oil-bearing seeds.

text.p: China's production of oil-bearing seeds for edible oil now falls far short of its production capacity due to the rapid construction of processing plants, officials and state media said on Tuesday.
China's annual edible oil production capacity has hit 50 million tonnes, while output of oil-bearing seeds stood at about 20 million tonnes, the official Economic Informarion Daily said.
"Many joint-venture oil processing factories have been set up in coastal areas to pursue high profits," an official of the State Grain Reserves Administration said by telephone.
China produced 22 million tonnes of edible oil-bearing seeds in 1996, including 10.1 million tonnes of peanuts and 9.1 million tonnes of rapeseed, official figures showed.
The country's annual consumption of edible vegetable oil was estimated at nine million tonnes, while domestic production was estimated at seven million tonnes, the newspaper said.
China's imports of edible vegetable oils including palm oil reached 2.64 million tonnes in 1996, down 25.3 percent compared with the year-ago, customs figures showed.
"Imports this year are unlikely to exceed the 1996 level," a second administration official said.

Many joint ventures that are supposed to be involved in processing, or import of semi-finished oil products for processing and re-exporting, sell their refined edible oil on the domestic market, the official said.
Oversupply of edible oil, also a result of rising smuggling, has depressed domestic prices in recent years, the official said, but declined to give further details.
